_comment: Parameter ranges and preset scenarios for the Mismatch Simulator. Persistence anchors are derived from the Conditioning Atlas (109 extracted experiments; see ../README.md for the provenance chain). Generated once by hand from atlas/merged.json and then maintained here — see scripts/refresh_atlas_anchors.py to recompute the evidence block.

units.stress: stress units; for thermal scenarios read 1 unit = 1 degree C above the local baseline

trend.label: Rate of environmental change
trend.note: 0.35 units/yr is roughly the pace of a fast-warming coastal system read as degrees C per year over a decade. 0 = a stationary environment with seasonality and noise only.

half_life.label: Memory half-life
half_life.note: Time for an induced state to decay halfway back to baseline in the absence of further stress. This is the parameter the Conditioning Atlas constrains best — and only as bounds, never as point estimates. See atlas_evidence below.

induction_rate.label: Induction rate
induction_rate.note: How fast memory accumulates while stress exceeds the induction threshold. The atlas rarely resolves this: most studies apply a fixed conditioning dose and measure the outcome later, without a time course during induction.

threshold.label: Induction threshold
threshold.note: Stress below this does not induce memory. Sublethal-but-suprathreshold conditioning is the atlas's inclusion criterion, so every atlas row sits above its own species' threshold by construction.

gain.label: Protective gain
gain.unit: stress units of tolerance shift per unit of memory
gain.note: How much the induced state actually shifts the phenotype's optimum. Gain is what makes memory worth having; cost is what makes it dangerous.

cost.label: Energetic cost of maintaining induction
cost.unit: fitness penalty per unit of memory per day (log scale)
cost.note: Couples to framework Question 7 (energetic cost of plasticity). Set to 0 to make memory free, in which case memory can be useless but never actively harmful — the trap collapses to mere inefficiency.

tolerance_width.label: Tolerance breadth
tolerance_width.note: Width of the Gaussian performance curve around the prepared-for stress level. Narrow breadth = a specialist that suffers badly from any mismatch.

noise.label: Environmental noise
noise.note: Unpredictable day-to-day variation. Noise is what makes a SHORT memory bad (it chases nothing); trend is what makes a LONG memory bad (it remembers a world that is gone). The interaction of the two is the whole point of the model.

seasonal_amplitude.label: Seasonal amplitude
seasonal_amplitude.note: Amplitude of an annual sinusoid. Predictable cycling is the case where anticipatory memory should pay off best.

inheritance.label: Transgenerational transfer
inheritance.note: Fraction of the parent's memory state carried into the offspring at each generation boundary. 0 = within-generation memory only. High transfer plus fast environmental change is the intergenerational form of the trap: parents priming offspring for a world that has already moved on.

generation_days.label: Generation time
generation_days.note: Only matters when transgenerational transfer is above zero.

years.label: Simulation length
years.note: Longer runs let a slow trend accumulate enough to cross the trap boundary.

presets.name: Coral thermal priming — short memory
presets.anchor_note: Louis et al. 2025 (Pocillopora damicornis, 7 d at +3 C) showed clear protection but the atlas records the induced state as already decaying across the ~8 d gap before challenge; Glass et al. 2023 (Nematostella) and Hazraty-Kari et al. 2023 (Acropora tenuis, gone by 28 d) also decayed. Half-life here is set to the short end of that bracket.

presets.name: Coral thermal priming — long memory
presets.anchor_note: Drury et al. 2022 (Montipora capitata) held a raised bleaching threshold 124 d after a 5 d pre-exposure; Wong et al. 2021 (Porites astreoides) saw effects across a year-long reciprocal transplant. Same taxon and stressor as the preset above, two orders of magnitude apart in persistence — the atlas genuinely does not resolve which is typical.

presets.name: Oyster immune priming
presets.anchor_note: Lafont et al. (Crassostrea gigas, single poly(I:C) injection) recorded 89-96% survival at every challenge timepoint out to 126-156 d post-priming, with no detected decay — so the true half-life is a lower bound, not a measurement. Immune priming is the atlas's longest-persisting within-generation memory.

presets.name: Oyster transgenerational pH conditioning
presets.anchor_note: Parker et al. 2015 (Saccostrea glomerata) carried a pCO2 history across F0-F1-F2 with improved acid-base regulation ~426 d out. Note that Venkataraman et al. 2019 (C. gigas) is scored 'Worsened' in the atlas over a comparable window — transgenerational pH conditioning is not reliably protective, which is exactly the ambiguity this preset is for.

presets.name: Urchin multigenerational — an observed trap
presets.anchor_note: Uthicke et al. (Echinometra sp. A) held F0 for 18 months and F1 for 25 months under near-future warming plus acidification; the ambient-ambient group ended up 21% larger and 31% faster at righting than every conditioned group. This is the atlas's clearest empirical instance of long-duration conditioning leaving animals worse off. The settings here are the model's attempt at that situation — long-lived state, high maintenance cost, slow generational turnover — and they do land in the trap. Note what it takes to get there: the trend has to be LOW. Push the rate of change above about 0.35 and the trap disappears, which is the model's central and least intuitive claim.

presets.name: Stationary world (memory should win)
presets.anchor_note: No directional trend, strong predictable seasonality. This is the control case: if anticipatory memory does not pay off here, something is wrong with the parameters (or the model).

atlas_evidence._comment: Persistence bounds by taxon and stressor from the Conditioning Atlas. CRITICAL: 'Persisted' means the effect was still detectable at the last timepoint tested, so longest_persisted_days is a LOWER bound on memory half-life, not an estimate of it. 'Decayed' means the effect was substantially gone by that timepoint, giving a rough UPPER bound. Most atlas rows tested a single timepoint, so these are censored observations and the true decay curves are almost entirely unmeasured — see README.md, 'What the atlas cannot tell us'.

observed_trap_instances._comment: Atlas rows scored direction='Worsened': experiments where conditioning left animals measurably worse off than unconditioned controls. 14 of 109 rows (13%). These are the empirical footprint of the trap this simulator models — the model does not need to be believed for these to be real.
